memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'"No descendant of Aaron the priest who has any defect is to come
near to present the food offerings to the LORD. He has a defect; he
must not come near to offer the food of his God. He may eat the most
holy food of his God, as well as the holy food"'" - Lev 21:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Do not miss this. The priest with a physical defect could not serve at
the altar - but he could still eat. He received the same holy food as
every other priest. He was not thrown out, not cut off, not left to
starve. He remained fully part of the priestly family and was provided
for from God's own table.

That single detail transforms how we read this passage. The
restriction was about a specific function, not about belonging. God
made sure the man was cared for.

There is real comfort here for anyone who cannot serve the way they
once did, or the way others do. Illness, age, disability, or
circumstances may limit what you can do. They do not limit what you
receive.

Paul writes that the body of Christ has many members with different
functions, and the parts that seem weaker are actually indispensable
(1 Cor 12:22). God has never measured a person by their usefulness.

Dear reader, if you feel sidelined today, hear this: you still eat at
the Father's table. Christ Himself is the bread of life (John 6:35),
and He is given freely to all who come.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I tied my worth to how much I can do for God?
2. Who around me feels sidelined and needs to be reminded they belong?
3. Am I feeding daily on Christ, or only serving?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that my place at Your table does not depend on my
usefulness. Feed my soul on Christ and remind me that I belong. Amen.
